mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous surge in earnings growth.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when accompanied by a simultaneous sharp decline in oil prices.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when accompanied by a simultaneous surge in export demand.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual monetary tightening and inflationary pressure, which erodes real corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a concurrent surge in commodity supply shocks.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 500 thousand units for four consecutive months signals a deepening housing market downturn, which reduces construction-related economic activity and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong mortgage rate declines.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a two-month period indicates labor market churning, which increases uncertainty and reduces corporate investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE also increases over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong wage growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals diminished household buffer capacity, which reduces discretionary spending and corporate revenue, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of rapid credit expansion.
